papers.title: Starfield: Demand-Aware Satellite Topology Design for Low-Earth Orbit Mega Constellations
papers.abstract: Low-Earth orbit (LEO) mega-constellations are emerging as high-capacity backbones for next-generation Internet. Deployment of laser terminals enables high-bandwidth, low-latency inter-satellite links (ISLs); however, their limited number, slow acquisition, and instability make forming a stable satellite topology difficult. Existing patterns like +Grid and Motif ignore regional traffic, ground station placement, and constellation geometry. Given sparse population distribution on Earth and the isolation of rural areas, traffic patterns are inherently non-uniform, providing an opportunity to orient inter-satellite links (ISLs) according to these traffic patterns. In this paper, we propose Starfield, a novel demand-aware satellite topology design heuristic algorithm supported by mathematical analysis. We first formulate a vector field on the constellation's shell according to traffic flows and define a corresponding Riemannian metric on the spherical manifold of the shell. The metric, combined with the spatial geometry, is used to assign a distance to each potential ISL, which we then aggregate over all demand flows to generate a score for each satellite's link selection. Inspired by +Grid, each satellite selects the link with the minimum Riemannian distance along with its corresponding angular links. To evaluate Starfield, we developed a custom, link-aware, and link-configurable packet-level simulator, comparing it against LAMP, +Grid, Motif, and Random topologies. For the Phase 1 Starlink, simulation results show up to a 30% reduction in hop count and a 15% improvement in stretch factor across multiple traffic distributions. Moreover, static Starfield, an inter-orbital link matching modification of Starfield, achieves a 15% improvement in stretch factor under realistic traffic patterns compared to +Grid. Experiments demonstrate Starfield's robustness under traffic demand perturbations.

papers.title: The Continuum Limit of the Deep Linear Network
papers.abstract: The Deep Linear Network (DLN) is a simple version of a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) in which the activation function is the identity and the bias vector is the zero vector. We examine the behavior of the model when the number of weight matrices, which is finite in the original model, goes to infinity. We show that a plausible continuum limit is a dimensionally reduced version of the Yang-Mills equation on the torus, revealing an unexpected geometric interpretation of infinite-depth DLNs. While we do not prove this rigorously, it is a very pretty calculation. It also gives some insight into several features of the construction. We note that the choices of boundary conditions on the ends of the discrete series survive better in the continuum limit. Also, the regularizing functional which uses the moment map survives nicely in the continuum limit, whereas the regularizing functional using the size of approximating terms has no sensible limit. This surely is useful information for the choices we make in the finite-dimensional theory, and might also be useful in the more complicated MLP setting.

papers.title: The classification of Fano contact manifolds revisited
papers.abstract: We present an account of the classification of Fano contact manifolds based on the proof of OpenAI and the solution of LeBrun-Salamon conjecture by Hu, Liu and Wan. The proof combines their constructions with earlier results on contact lines, with some simplifications.

papers.title: Logarithmic Sobolev and exponential inequalities for submanifolds in Cartan--Hadamard manifolds
papers.abstract: We establish a logarithmic Sobolev inequality for complete $C^{1,1}$ immersed submanifolds of dimension $m\ge2$ in Cartan--Hadamard manifolds with sectional curvature at most $-b^2$. The inequality retains the Euclidean sharp constant after subtraction of $(m-1)^2b^2$ from the Fisher and mean-curvature energy; this coefficient is maximal for a lower bound uniform over $b\ge0$. For immersed surfaces, we prove both a finite-domain critical exponential inequality and a global Ruf-type inequality with a positive $L^2$ term. Both have potential $|H|^2-b^2$, exponent $16\pi$ and an absolute multiplicative constant, and follow from one geometric heat-kernel comparison. The exponent and curvature coefficient are optimal. We classify Gaussian equality in the logarithmic inequality and geometric equality in the higher-dimensional Nash consequence. All inequality constants are independent of the codimension.

papers.title: Chern scalar curvature and finite-time singularities of the conformal Chern--Calabi flow
papers.abstract: On every unit-volume flat complex three-torus, we construct a solution of the volume-preserving conformal Chern--Calabi flow with a finite-time Chern Type-I singularity at any prescribed point. The full spatial supremum has an exact asymptotic coefficient, and prescribed rescalings converge to a complete nonflat radial shrinking solution. The positive part of Chern scalar curvature can remain arbitrarily small throughout the flow, as can each prescribed subcritical spatial curvature norm. We determine the punctured terminal metric, its one-point completion and unique nonflat tangent cone, and the terminal energy asymptotics. We also exclude Chern Type-II under a logarithmically improved critical weak $L^3$ bound on Chern scalar curvature, and prove a separate scale-invariant integral criterion involving first Chern--Ricci curvature. The constructed singular solutions satisfy both criteria.

papers.title: The dual Orlicz-Minkowski problem for capillary hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We study curvature flows for the dual Orlicz--Minkowski problem for strictly convex capillary hypersurfaces in the Euclidean half-space. The prescribed function has the form $\phi(h)G(X)$, where $X=\nabla h+h\nu$ and $G$ may be nonradial and nonhomogeneous. For acute contact angles, the evenness assumption together with either of the two integral conditions yields a smooth weighted-volume-preserving flow for all $t>0$ and a smooth solution to the dual Orlicz--Minkowski equation. Without the evenness assumption, two strict spherical-cap barriers yield the same conclusions for an unnormalized flow, whose limiting hypersurfaces solve the dual Orlicz--Minkowski equation with $c=1$. A uniform strict monotonicity condition under rescaling ensures uniqueness for $c=1$ and convergence of the unnormalized flow in any $C^k$ norm at an exponential rate. The problem considered here includes the capillary $L_p$-Minkowski and $L_p$ dual Minkowski problems as special cases.

papers.title: Capillary $L_p$ dual Minkowski flow
papers.abstract: For $n\geq2$ and $\theta\in(0,\pi/2)$, we study the long-time existence and asymptotic behavior of an even normalized capillary $L_p$ dual Minkowski flow in the Euclidean half-space $\overline{\mathbb{R}^{n+1}_+}$. When $pq\geq0$, the flow exists for all positive time and the evolving hypersurfaces converge smoothly along a sequence of times tending to infinity to a stationary solution of the normalized problem. If $p\neq q$, a dilation of the limit solves the unnormalized problem.

papers.title: Hodge--Riemann relations for $m$-positive and generalized $m$-positive forms
papers.abstract: We study Hodge--Riemann relations for ordinary, sequential, and weak $m$-positive real $(1,1)$-forms in complex dimension $d$. For ordinary $m$-positive forms, we prove the fully mixed relations in every permitted bidegree without assuming semipositivity, generalizing results by Xiao. As a generalization of ordinary $m$-positivity, sequential $m$-positivity is defined by the hyperbolicity cones of successive directional derivatives of the determinant. We formulate a generalized mixed Hodge--Riemann conjecture for this condition and prove several cases beyond the scalar inequalities supplied by hyperbolicity. We also consider weak $m$-positivity which corresponds to the pointwise subsolution condition for the complex $m$-Hessian equation. In this setting, we prove the Hodge--Riemann relations for $p\neq q$ and in several diagonal cases, and show that the associated power map induces a pointwise diffeomorphism onto the cone of positive $(d-1,d-1)$-forms. Using Dinh and Nguy\^en's $L^2$ globalization method, we pass from the pointwise relations to cohomology classes on compact K\"ahler manifolds. Finally, we propose conjectures on a numerical criterion for sequential positivity and on solvability of the generalized $m$-Hessian equation.

papers.title: Human Variations on AI Mathematics
papers.abstract: This article is motivated by the OpenAI manuscripts "Minimal metrics and interior injectivity for nef adjoints" and "Log abundance in characteristic zero". We establish a jet comparison for metrics with minimal singularities and use it to prove a dlt-type extension theorem. Combined with geometric arguments from the latter manuscript, this yields an alternative analytic proof of its Theorem~3.1.

papers.title: On a Class of Non-Local Elliptic-Transport Systems in Score-Guided Probability Flow on $SE(3)$: Score-Singularity Resolution, Space-Time ADN Shift, and Markov Mean-Field Games
papers.abstract: We establish mathematical foundations for optimal spatiotemporal vector fields governing continuous score-guided probability flows over bounded submanifolds $M \subset SE(3)$ on the Special Euclidean group $SE(3) \cong \mathbb{R}^3 \times SO(3)$. Modeling dynamic density evolution via a score-perturbed Lie-algebraic continuity equation under zero-flux boundary conditions, we resolve the non-local score drift singularity $s(g,t) = \nabla_{SE(3)} \log \rho(g,t)$ as $\rho \rightarrow 0^+$ via weighted parabolic flux dissipation bounds. Using left-invariant exponential group mollifiers, we derive boundary-preserving DiPerna--Lions commutator estimates tracking structure constants $\{c_{ij}^k\}$. Second, interpreting the optimality system as a 7D space-time elliptic operator $L_{7D} = -\Delta_{SE(3)} - \partial_t^2$ with zero-order corner compatibility on $\partial M \times \{0,T\}$, we establish Agmon--Douglis--Nirenberg $W_p^2(Q_T)$ shift estimates tracking Lie algebra constants, boundary geometry $\|\partial M\|_{C^2}$, and Ricci curvature $\|Ric_{SE(3)}\|_{L^\infty}$, yielding a full $C^\infty(\overline{Q}_T)$ Schauder bootstrap expansion. Third, we extend this system to non-cooperative Markov Mean-Field Games (MFGs) on $SE(3)$, establishing score-guided Nash equilibria via Schauder--Tychonoff fixed points. Crucially, the constant diagonal Ricci curvature $Ric_{SE(3)} = \mathrm{diag}(0,0,0,1/2,1/2,1/2)$ from $SO(3)$ induces a sharp Bochner--Weitzenb\"ock spectral gap boost $\lambda_1(-\Delta_{SE(3)}) \ge \lambda_1(-\Delta_{\mathbb{R}^3}) + 1/2 > 0$. This positive rotational curvature enhances the Lie-algebraic Poincar\'e coercivity constant, demonstrating that intrinsic group curvature stabilizes score-guided flows against dispersion and expands the critical Nash uniqueness horizon $T_{SE(3)}^*$ beyond flat Euclidean limits.

papers.title: Quantitative finiteness for maximal complex totally geodesic submanifolds of non-arithmetic ball quotients
papers.abstract: We prove that the number of maximal complex totally geodesic submanifolds of a smooth finite-volume non-arithmetic ball quotient is bounded linearly by its volume, with a constant depending only on the complex dimension. This gives a quantitative strengthening of the finiteness theorems of Bader--Fisher--Miller--Stover (Invent. Math., 2023) and Baldi--Ullmo (Ann. of Math., 2023).

papers.title: Blowdowns along Ricci flow in dimension four
papers.abstract: We show that the blowdown shrinking Ricci soliton of Feldman, Ilmanen and Knopf is strictly dynamically stable in the following strong local sense: (1) The Ricci flow from every metric on a closed 4-manifold containing a region close to a rescaling of a sufficiently large compact subset of the soliton in either orientation and with controlled geometry elsewhere develops a singularity with unique tangent flow modeled on the soliton. (2) The singular time slice has an isolated conical singularity, and by Gianniotis-Schulze the flow can be continued by blowing down a sphere of self-intersection $\pm1$. (3) On a closed 4-manifold, the set of metrics whose Ricci flows have their first singularity modeled on the soliton is $C^{14}$-open. It is nonempty if and only if the manifold contains a sphere of self-intersection $\pm1$. (4) The soliton is strongly rigid among shrinking Ricci solitons. As applications, we construct $C^{14}$-open sets of initial data whose Ricci flows perform any prescribed ordered sequence of blowdowns. (1) Every closed simply connected smooth 4-manifold, including spin and exotic examples, can be reached by Ricci flow from a standard $k\mathbb{CP}^2\#\ell\overline{\mathbb{CP}}{}^2$, through finitely many blowdown singularities. (2) On the standard $2\mathbb{CP}^{2}\#9\overline{\mathbb{CP}}{}^{2}$, there are infinitely many open sets of initial metrics whose Ricci flows, after a single blowdown, reach pairwise nondiffeomorphic manifolds. The proof uses the spectral analysis of Naff and the second author and deals with the gauge-fixing problem along Ricci flow through a Wa\.zewski argument inspired by Stolarski. We also use Bamler-Lai's PDE-ODI principle. Except for continuation (requiring nonnegative curvature of the asymptotic cone), all results apply to linearly stable nonflat asymptotically conical shrinkers in all dimensions.

papers.title: Spectral and convex geometry of $\alpha$-harmonic maps and sharp Morse index rigidity
papers.abstract: We develop a weighted scalar spectral geometric description of Sacks-Uhlenbeck $\alpha$-harmonic maps into round spheres and identify its convex geometry realization for $\alpha$-harmonic diffeomorphisms onto the round $2$-sphere. More precisely, we establish a one-to-one correspondence, modulo orientation preserving isometries of $\mathbb{S}^2$, between orientation preserving $\alpha$-harmonic diffeomorphisms onto the round $2$-sphere and positive Codazzi tensors satisfying a determinant bound and a compatibility condition with the prescribed metric on $\mathbb{S}^2$. These tensors are the radii tensors of auxiliary strictly convex surfaces, and the weighted scalar forms in spectral geometry equal $-\alpha$ times the second variations of the enclosed volumes with respect to the support functions. Using these spectral geometry and convex geometry results, we prove a sharp Morse index characterization of isometric equatorial parametrizations among $\alpha$-harmonic $2$-spheres in the round $n$-sphere. We also prove that every $\alpha$-harmonic diffeomorphism between unit round $2$-spheres is orthogonal for all $\alpha>1$. Equivalently, the only admissible positive Codazzi tensor whose reconstructed metric on $\mathbb{S}^2$ has Gaussian curvature $1$ is $(\kappa+2)^{\alpha-1}\bar{g}$, where $\bar{g}$ is the unit round metric.

papers.title: On the Local Regularity of Homogeneous Complex Monge-Amp\`ere Equations
papers.abstract: We establish a local higher regularity theorem for the homogeneous complex Monge-Ampere equation on $X\times D$, where $X$ is a complete, possibly noncompact Kahler manifold and $D\subset\mathbb C$ is the unit disc. For a bounded weak solution given by the Perron envelope, we prove higher regularity on a smaller spatial domain when the smooth boundary data are locally small. The geometric hypotheses require uniformly convex local Kahler potentials and a local barrier threshold sufficiently large relative to the global $L^\infty$ bound of the solution. We also obtain quantitative local Holder estimates. The proof combines a perturbative construction of local holomorphic disc foliations with a construction of global subsolutions using convexity and barriers. A key analytic difficulty is the loss of Holder regularity in the construction of holomorphic disc families, which we address using BMO estimates and Nash-Moser-Zehnder theorems. Comparison along the discs identifies the local smooth solution by holomorphic discs foliation with the global weak solution. We apply the theorem and its proof to compact Kahler manifolds and to ALE, ALF, and asymptotically complex hyperbolic (ACH) ends. Under the stated geometric and decay assumptions, we obtain higher regularity of each prescribed order sufficiently far out, together with weighted Holder estimates preserving the boundary decay.

papers.title: Degenerate neckpinches at the first $N$ singular times
papers.abstract: For every integer $N\ge1$, we construct a smooth closed connected strictly mean-convex rotationally symmetric surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose level set flow remains connected until extinction and has exactly one singular point at each of its first $N$ singular times. These singularities are degenerate neckpinches with the Angenent--Vel\'azquez asymptotics: the leading deviation from the cylinder under parabolic rescaling is a cubic Hermite term.

papers.title: Cosmological rigidity via $p$-harmonic temporal functions
papers.abstract: We prove a splitting theorem for cosmological spacetimes which admit a globally $p$-harmonic Cauchy temporal function for some $p < 1$, without making any use of timelike lines. In Bartnik's context of cosmological and timelike geodesically complete spacetimes, we establish a Liouville-type unboundedness result which shows that globally $p$-harmonic temporal functions, $p < 1$, are necessarily Cauchy temporal. Moreover, using the theory of elliptic PDEs, we show that locally Lipschitz $p$-harmonic temporal functions with $p < 1$ are in fact smooth. Altogether, our work reduces the resolution of Bartnik's cosmological splitting conjecture to the global weak solvability of the $p$-d'Alembert equation for some $p < 1$ in the class of locally Lipschitz temporal functions.

papers.title: Double Fibration Transforms: Geometry and Microlocal Analysis
papers.abstract: Double fibration transforms integrate functions over families of submanifolds. We survey the recovery of singularities by both classical normal operator methods and direct analytic methods. We also discuss support theorems, injectivity and applications to geodesic ray transforms, seismic inversion and minimal surface data.

papers.title: A Reilly approach to weighted curvature integral inequalities in hyperbolic space
papers.abstract: We establish a polarized weighted Reilly identity and an exact deficit decomposition for weighted curvature integrals $I_j=\int_\Sigma VE_j~\mathrm{d}\mu$ in hyperbolic space, where $V=\cosh r$ and $E_j$ is the normalized $j$th mean curvature. For compact domains with smooth connected boundary, these yield $I_k^2\geq I_{k-1}I_{k+1}$ under intrinsic sub-staticity at $k=1$ and static convexity with $\kappa\in\Gamma_k\cap\overline{\Gamma}_{k+1}$ for $2\leq k\leq n-1$, with equality precisely for geodesic balls. Under $h\geq0$ and $Vh-V_\nu g\geq0$, log-concavity and a Euclidean mixed-volume representation recover the centered-ball comparisons conjectured by Hu and Li \cite[Conjecture~1.1]{HuLi}, allowing the weight center to lie outside the domain. Equality in these comparisons holds precisely for balls centered at the weight center.

papers.title: Limiting properties of Hermitian-Einstein metrics under variation of the K\"ahler class
papers.abstract: We study the behaviour of Hermitian-Einstein metrics on a holomorphic vector bundle over a compact K\"ahler manifold, as the underlying K\"ahler metric varies and its K\"ahler class changes. In particular, if the bundle stops being stable at some point, the Hermitian-Einstein metrics blow up, and their rescaling can be used to construct a destabilizing subsheaf, following the argument of Uhlenbeck and Yau. Furthermore, we study the behaviour of Chern connections of these metrics, and show, that after passing to a subsequence, and applying suitable gauge transforms these connections converge, and identify the blow-up locus of their Uhlenbeck limit.

papers.title: Flexibility of Laplace-Beltrami eigenfunctions under metric variation
papers.abstract: We study the surjectivity of the differential of the Laplace-Beltrami operator with respect to the metric parameter. We use the obtained results to prove that every small deformation of a nonconstant eigenfunction can be realized with a small perturbation of the metric. As a consequence, we prove that every generic property of smooth functions which is invariant under multiplication by a nonzero scalar is generic for eigenfunctions of the Laplace-Beltrami operator, extending a result by Uhlenbeck.

papers.title: Free boundary minimal annuli in convex balls
papers.abstract: We construct a $4$-parameter family of properly embedded genus-zero surfaces with at most two boundary components in a Riemannian $3$-ball. The construction is a free boundary analog of the canonical $5$-parameter family of surfaces on the $3$-sphere by Marques-Neves in the proof of Willmore conjecture. In the Euclidean unit ball, this family realizes the critical catenoid as a Simon-Smith min-max limit. As applications, we give an upper bound of Almgren-Pitts $4$-width $\omega_4(\mathbb{B}^3)$ by the area of the critical catenoid. Moreover, we prove the existence of at least three free boundary minimal annuli in any compact $3$-manifold with nonnegative Ricci curvature and strictly convex boundary.

papers.title: Negatively Curved Minimal Surfaces in the Round Four-Sphere
papers.abstract: We construct smooth closed embedded minimal surfaces with everywhere negative Gaussian curvature in the unit round four-sphere. More precisely, for every sufficiently large integer $m$, our construction gives a minimal surface $\Sigma_m$ of genus $m^2+1$ such that $\operatorname{Area}(\Sigma_m)\to 4\pi^2$ as $m\to+\infty$. This result yields a complete solution to Problem 101 in Yau's 1982 list of open problems.

papers.title: Understanding entropy using Aubin--Yau deformations
papers.abstract: In this paper we investigate three types of entropy that frequently appear in the research of K\"ahler geometry: the classical K\"ahler entropy, the radial entropy and the non-Archimedean entropy. We give a unifying interpretation for these entropies by showing that they can all be expressed as the derivative of the Monge--Amp\`ere energy along certain Aubin--Yau type deformations. Such considerations also lead to a novel algebraic criterion for the existence of constant scalar curvature K\"ahler metrics.

papers.title: Four-Dimensional Semi-Homogeneous Convex Cones: A Complete Classification
papers.abstract: We classify all four-dimensional semi-homogeneous convex cones, i.e., closed, pointed, full-dimensional cones whose connected automorphism group has principal orbits of codimension at most one. On such cones, the Monge-Amp\`ere equation defining the canonical barrier reduces to an ordinary differential equation. This makes this barrier computationally accessible. The semi-homogeneous cones can then be used in modeling by conic programs. An obvious subset of such cones are the homogeneous cones. The key point allowing the classification is that for all other cones, the automorphism group has a three-dimensional subgroup acting locally faithfully on the principal orbits. This subgroup must have a Lie algebra which is either abelian or a direct product of a 1-dimensional algebra and a two-dimensional algebra generated by $A,B$ satisfying $[A,B]=B$. In both cases we classify all 4-dimensional representations up to isomorphism, and for each representation all invariant convex cones. For every cone an orbit invariant is computed.

papers.title: Noncritical multi-bubbles and hyperbolic double bubbles
papers.abstract: We prove that standard $k$-bubbles uniquely minimize perimeter in $\mathbb R^n$ and $\mathbb S^n$ for $n\ge2$ and $1\le k\le n$, and that standard double bubbles uniquely minimize perimeter in $\mathbb H^n$ for $n\ge3$. For nonnegative curvature, the proof combines the structure and spectral theory of Milman--Neeman with a uniform semialgebraic exceptional set, an almost-everywhere profile comparison, and localized variational arguments. A curvature-variable lift gives a uniformly elliptic comparison at the Euclidean limit. The independent hyperbolic argument uses the rotational structure of Cotton--Freeman, a scalar meridian force potential, and a transverse conformal variation. The critical range $k=n+1$ in $\mathbb R^n$ and $\mathbb S^n$, and hyperbolic clusters with more than two finite cells, are not covered.

papers.title: A Koszul-Type Splitting Theorem for Complex Supermanifolds
papers.abstract: We study the splitting problem for complex supermanifolds using formal exponential maps and Ehresmann connections. We show that every formal exponential map induces a splitting of the underlying supermanifold. Furthermore, we establish that every Ehresmann connection determines a linearization of the infinite jet space, extending the corresponding construction for ordinary manifolds to supermanifolds. For Ehresmann connections preserving the zero section, we construct a formal exponential map in two ways: via the linearization of the infinite jet space and directly from the connection operator. We prove that both constructions yield the same map and induce the same splitting, thereby generalizing Koszul's splitting theorem from linear connections to zero-section-preserving Ehresmann connections. Finally, we provide examples showing that, without this assumption, the two constructions may yield different splittings, or one or both of them may fail to induce a splitting.

papers.title: Coisotropy-one homogeneous spacetimes I: (3,2)-Kinematical Lie algebras with $d\geq 3$
papers.abstract: This is the first of several papers devoted to the classification of coisotropy-one homogeneous spacetimes. It is the first step in extending the classification of spatially isotropic homogeneous spacetimes of kinematical Lie groups to the much vaster context of homogeneous spacetimes that are not spatially isotropic; that is, where the rotations no longer act transitively on the space of directions in each tangent space. In this first paper we classify (up to isomorphisms preserving the rotational subalgebra) a class of the relevant transitive Lie algebras, the so-called (3,2)-kinematical Lie algebras, for the coisotropy-one case in spatial dimension at least 4. As a by-product of this classification, we classify two-dimensional real representations of Bianchi Lie algebras up to a suitable notion of equivalence.

papers.title: A closed formula for the Poisson cohomology of scalar Dubrovin-Novikov brackets in arbitrary dimension
papers.abstract: The structure of the Poisson cohomology groups for scalar Poisson brackets of Dubrovin-Novikov type with $D$ independent variables has been first described in arXiv:1512.05744 ; in that work, a complete dimensional counting was provided for $D=2$, and some numerical results exhibited for $D=3$, $D=4$. Here, we prove a formula for the dimensional counting of the Poisson cohomology for arbitrary $D$. Moreover, we show how to obtain canonical representatives for each cohomology class.

papers.title: Spatial degeneracy along weak geodesics in the space of K\"ahler potentials
papers.abstract: We study spatial Hessian degeneracy along weak K\"ahler geodesics. We construct examples in three settings: (1) On every compact K\"ahler manifold, the spatial form degenerates on a nonempty open set during an interior time interval, although both endpoints are smooth and strictly K\"ahler. (2) On ALE K\"ahler manifolds with a holomorphic quotient end and a decaying potential to the Euclidean metric, spatial degeneracy occurs on open regions arbitrarily far along an unbounded horn. (3) For cone and Poincar\'e endpoint metrics along a smooth divisor, normal spatial degeneracy occurs on open sets approaching the divisor. Both cone endpoints retain the prescribed angle. The first construction answers negatively the spatial-positivity question recorded in Darvas's survey. The ALE and divisor constructions show that weak geodesics need not preserve the asymptotic behavior of the endpoint metrics.

papers.title: Biunital Lie Semiheaps and Lie Triple Systems
papers.abstract: We examine the differential geometry of Lie semiheaps that admit biunital elements. Open Ol'shanskii semigroups, which appear widely across causal geometry and harmonic analysis, provide a large class of examples. It is shown that the subset of biunits is a smoothly embedded Lie subheap. Moreover, there is a canonical Lie triple algebroid associated with any proper biunital Lie semiheap. That is, there is a vector bundle over the manifold of biunits that comes equipped with a ternary bracket that satisfies the axioms of a Lie triple system together with a compatible `higher' anchor map. Although every Lie triple algebroid associated with a proper biunital Lie semiheap is trivialisable, it is not canonically so, unlike the case of the tangent bundle of a Lie group. As concrete examples, we examine the Lie semiheap of real $n\times n$ matrices, and the conformal causal Lie semiheap associated with the Lie group $\mathrm{SU}(2,2)$, which is a double cover of the conformal group of Minkowski spacetime, and the future-directed light cone.
